akhfash:2-2.t: As for the saying of [Allah] the Mighty and Majestic ﴿وَأَجَلٌ مُّسمًّى عِندَهُ﴾, ﴿أَجَلٌ﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and is not [conjoined] to [the object of] ﴿قَضَىۤ﴾.

akhfash:6-6.t: [Allah the Exalted said] ﴿أَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَبْلِهِم مِّن قَرْنٍ مَّكَّنَّاهُمْ﴾, then He said ﴿مَا لَمْ نُمَكِّن لَّكُمْ﴾: it is as if He informed the Prophet ﷺ and then addressed him together with them, as He said ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا كُنتُمْ فِي ٱلْفُلْكِ وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِم﴾, bringing the third-person form while He was addressing [them], because he is the one addressed.

akhfash:12-12.t: And He said: ﴿كَتَبَ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ ٱلرَّحْمَةَ لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ﴾: the lām of ﴿لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ﴾ has fatḥa because, given the meaning of "كَتَبَ" (He prescribed), it is as if He said "by Allah, He will surely gather you". Then He substituted, saying ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ خَسِرُوۤاْ أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾, i.e. He will surely gather those who have lost themselves.

akhfash:14-14.t:
[And He said] ﴿أَغَيْرَ ٱللَّهِ أَتَّخِذُ وَلِيّاً فَاطِرِ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾ as a naʿt (adjective). Some read ﴿فاطرُ﴾ in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ [i.e. a new start], i.e. He is the Originator.
And some read ﴿وهو يُطْعِمُ ولا يَطْعَم﴾, and some read ﴿ولا يُطْعَمُ﴾; and ﴿يَطْعَمُ﴾ is the [proper] way, because you only say "هُوَ يُطْعَمُ" (he is fed) of one who eats, so you inform [us] that He does not eat anything. And ﴿يُطْعَمُ﴾ is only read because people agree on it. [Translator's note: the passage is as written; the two statements about ﴿يَطْعَمُ﴾ and ﴿يُطْعَمُ﴾ appear inconsistent, possibly through copying errors.]
And He said ﴿إِنِّيۤ أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَلاَ تَكُونَنَّ﴾, i.e. and it was said to me: "do not be". ﴿أُمِرْتُ﴾ became a substitute for that, because when he said ﴿أُمِرْتُ﴾ he informed [us] that it had been said to him.

akhfash:23-23.t:
And He said ﴿ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ فِتْنَتُهُمْ إِلاَّ أَن قَالُواْ وَٱللَّهِ رَبِّنَا﴾ as a ṣifa (qualifier). Some read ﴿رَبَّنا﴾ in the sense of "O our Lord". As for ﴿واللهِ﴾, it is genitive as an oath; if there were no wāw in it, you would put it in the accusative and say "اللهَ رَبَّنا". Some of them use the genitive without the wāw because this name is so frequently used, but this is poor by analogy. The like of it has come irregularly, in their saying [in the rajaz metre; this is the one hundred and eighty-ninth shāhid]:
* وَبَلَدٍ عامِيَّةٍ أَعْماؤُهُ *
(And many a land whose blind wastes are trackless.)
[And] it is only "رُبَّ بَلَدٍ" (many a land). And he said [in the wāfir metre; this is the one hundred and ninetieth shāhid]:
نَهَيْتُكَ عَنْ طِلابِكَ أُمَّ عَمْرٍو * بِعاقِبَةٍ وَأَنْت إِذٍ صَحِيحُ
(I forbade you from pursuing Umm ʿAmr in good time, while you were then healthy.)
He means "حِينَئِدٍ" (at that time): he dropped "حينَ" and left it implied. And the wāw became a substitute for "رُبَّ" in "وَبَلَدٍ". They may also put "بَلْ" in this position. The poet said [in the rajaz metre; this is the one hundred and ninety-first shāhid]:
ما بالُ عَيْنٍ عَنْ كَراها قَدْ جَفَتْ * مُسْبِلَةً تَسْتَنُّ لَمّا عَرَفَتْ
داراً لِلَيْلى بَعْدَ حَوْلٍ قَدْ عَفَتْ * بَلْ جَوْزِ تَيْهاءَ كَظَهْرِ الحَجَفَتْ
(What is the matter with an eye that has shunned its sleep, flowing and pouring when it recognised an abode of Laylā, effaced after a year? — Nay, many a middle of a trackless desert like the back of a leather shield.)
[this is] according to those who say "طَلَحَتْ" [i.e. pronounce the feminine ending as tāʾ in pause].

akhfash:25-25.t:
[And] He said: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً أَن يَفْقَهُوهُ وَفِيۤ آذَانِهِمْ وَقْراً﴾. The singular of "الأَكِنَّة" is "الكِنان" (covering). "الوَقْر" in the ear is [with fatḥa], and "الوِقْر" on the back (a load) is with kasra. Yūnus said: "I asked Ruʾba", and he said: "وَقِرَتْ أُذُنُهُ", "تَوْقَرُ", when there is "الوَقْر" (deafness) in it. Abū Zayd said: "I heard the Arabs say 'أُذُنٌ مَوْقُورَةٌ' (a deafened ear)", so this one says "وُقِرَتْ". The poet said [in the ramal metre; this is the one hundred and ninety-second shāhid]:
وَكلامٍ سَيِّىءٍ قَدْ وُقِرَتْ * أُذُنِي مِنْهُ وَما بِي مِنْ صَمَمْ
(And many an evil word from which my ear has been made deaf, though I have no deafness.)
And He said ﴿أَسَاطِيرُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ﴾. Some claim that its singular is "أُسْطُورَة" and some "إِسّطارَة"; but I consider it only one of the plurals that have no singular, like "عَبادِيد" (scattered groups), "مَذاكِير" and "أَبابِيل" (flocks). Some said the singular of "الأَبابيل" is "إبِّيل", and some said "إِبَّوْل", like "عِجَّوْل"; but I did not find the Arabs knowing a singular for it. As for "الشَّماطِيط" (scattered pieces), they claim its singular is "شِمْطاط". All of these have a singular, except that it is not used and has not been spoken, because this pattern occurs only as a plural. I heard the eloquent Arabs say "أَرْسَلَ إِبِلَهُ أَبابيلَ" (he sent off his camels in flocks), meaning "groups", and no singular has been spoken for it.

akhfash:26-26.t: As for His saying: ﴿وَيَنْأَوْنَ عَنْهُ﴾, it is from "نَأَيْتُ", "يَنْأَى", "نَأْياً" (to keep far away).

akhfash:27-27.t: And He said: ﴿وَلاَ نُكَذِّبَ بِآيَاتِ رَبِّنَا وَنَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ — accusative because it is the answer to a wish, and what follows the wāw is like what follows the fāʾ. And if you wish, you put it in the nominative and treat it like an oath, as if they said "and we will not — by Allah — deny the signs of our Lord, and we will be — by Allah — among the believers". This is when this line is cut off from the first. The nominative is the [proper] way of speech, and that is how we read the verse. [And] when one puts it in the accusative, he makes it a wāw of conjunction, as though they had wished not to deny and to be [among the believers]. And this — Allah knows best — is not the case, because they did not wish for faith; they only wished to be sent back, and they declared that they would not deny and would be among the believers.

akhfash:31-31.t: And He said ﴿أَلاَ سَآءَ مَا يَزِرُونَ﴾, because it is from "وَزَرَ", "يَزِرُ", "وِزْراً" (to bear a burden). One also says "وُزِرَ", so "هُوَ مَوْزُورٌ" (he is burdened). Yūnus claimed that both are said.

akhfash:33-33.t: And He said ﴿قَدْ نَعْلَمُ إِنَّهُ لَيَحْزُنُكَ﴾ with kasra on "إِنَّ" because of the entry of the additional lām after it.

akhfash:34-34.t: And He said ﴿وَلَقدْ جَآءَكَ مِن نَّبَإِ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾, as you say "قَدْ أَصَابَنا من مَطَرٍ" (some rain has fallen on us) and "قَدْ كانَ مِنْ حَديث" (there has been some talk).

akhfash:35-35.t:
And He said ﴿نَفَقاً فِي ٱلأَرْضِ أَوْ سُلَّماً فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾: "النَفَق" is not from "النَفقَة" (expenditure) but from "النَّافِقاء" (the jerboa's burrow exit); He means a way into the earth.
And He said ﴿فَإِن ٱسْتَطَعْتَ أَن تَبْتَغِيَ نَفَقاً فِي ٱلأَرْضِ أَوْ سُلَّماً فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾ and did not say "then do it"; that is because He left it implied. The poet said [in the khafīf metre; this is the one hundred and thirty-second shāhid]: [Translator's note: the number is as written; the sequence here would lead one to expect the one hundred and ninety-third.]
فَبِحَظٍّ مِمّا نَعِيشُ ولا تَذْ * هَبْ بِكِ التُرَّهاتِ في الأَهْوالِ
(So [live] with a share of what we live on, and let not vain fancies carry you off into perils.)
He left "فَعِيشى" (so live) implied.

akhfash:38-38.t: And He said ﴿وَلاَ طَائِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيْهِ إِلاَّ أُمَمٌ أَمْثَالُكُمْ﴾: He means the plural of "أمة" (community).

akhfash:40-40.t: And He said ﴿أَرَأَيْتَكُم إِنْ أَتَاكُمْ عَذَابُ ٱللَّهِ أَوْ أَتَتْكُمْ ٱلسَّاعَةُ أَغَيْرَ ٱللَّهِ تَدْعُونَ﴾: what follows the tāʾ in His saying ﴿أَرَأَيْتَكُم﴾ came only for address, and the tāʾ was left with fatḥa as it is for the singular. It is like the kāf of "رُوَيْدَكَ زَيْداً" (go easy on Zayd) when you say "أَرْوِدْ زَيْداً". This kāf has no [grammatical] position to be called genitive, nominative or accusative; it is only [a sign] of address, like the kāf of "ذاك". Like that is the Arabs' saying "أَبْصِرْكَ زَيْداً": they put in the kāf for address, and it is only "أَبْصِرْ زيداً" (look at Zayd).

akhfash:46-46.t: And He said ﴿أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَخَذَ ٱللَّهُ سَمْعَكُمْ وَأَبْصَارَكُمْ﴾, then He said ﴿يَأْتِيكُمْ بِهِ﴾: He referred it to "hearing", or to what was taken from them.

akhfash:52-52.t: And He said ﴿فَتَطْرُدَهُمْ فَتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ﴾: the first is accusative as an answer to His saying ﴿مَا عَلَيْكَ مِنْ حِسَابِهِم مِّن شَيْءٍ وَمَا مِنْ حِسَابِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّن شَيْءٍ فَتَطْرُدَهُمْ﴾, and the other is accusative by His saying ﴿وَلاَ تَطْرُدِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ﴾ ﴿فَتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ﴾.

akhfash:54-54.t: And He said: ﴿كَتَبَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ ٱلرَّحْمَةَ أَنَّهُ مَن عَمِلَ﴾ and ﴿أَنَّهُ مَن عَمِلَ مِنكُمْ سُوۤءًا بِجَهَالَةٍ ثُمَّ تَابَ مِن بَعْدِهِ وَأَصْلَحَ فَأَنَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾. His saying ﴿أَنَّهُ﴾ is a badal (substitute) from His saying ﴿ٱلرَّحْمَةَ﴾, i.e. He prescribed that whoever does [evil]… And His saying ﴿فَأِنَّهُ﴾ [with kasra] is as a new start, i.e. then for him is forgiveness and mercy, for He is Forgiving, Merciful. Some read ﴿فأنَّهُ﴾ [with fatḥa], meaning by it the noun and leaving the khabar (predicate) implied; he meant "فَأنَّ" (then [it is a fact] that…).

akhfash:55-55.t: And He said ﴿وَلِتَسْتَبِينَ سَبِيلُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ [with tāʾ], because the people of the Ḥijāz say "هِيَ السَّبِيلُ" (the way, feminine). Some read ﴿ولتستبين﴾* meaning [you,] the Prophet ﷺ. And some read ﴿وَلِيَسْتَبِينَ سَبِيلُ﴾ [with yāʾ] in the dialect of the Banū Tamīm.

akhfash:56-56.t: And He said ﴿قَدْ ضَلَلْتُ إِذاً﴾, and some read ﴿ضَلَلْتُ﴾; they are two dialect forms. Whoever says "ضَلِلْتُ" says "تَضَلُّ", and whoever says "ضَلَلْتُ" says "تَضِلُّ". We read it with the fatḥa*. [Translator's note: both quotations are written identically; the second was evidently meant to be «ضَلِلْتُ».]

akhfash:59-59.t: And He said ﴿وَمَا تَسْقُطُ مِن وَرَقَةٍ إِلاَّ يَعْلَمُهَا وَلاَ حَبَّةٍ فِي ظُلُمَاتِ ٱلأَرْضِ وَلاَ رَطْبٍ وَلاَ يَابِسٍ إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾: genitive by [conjunction to what follows] ﴿مِنْ﴾; if you wish, you put it in the nominative [by conjunction to the subject of] "تسقط"; and if you wish, you make it a new start (mubtadaʾ) and cut it off from the first.

akhfash:63-63.t: And He said ﴿تَدْعُونَهُ تَضَرُّعاً وَخُفْيَةً﴾, and He said in another place ﴿وَخِيفَةً﴾. "الخُفْيَة" is concealment, and "الخِيفَة" is from fear and dread.

akhfash:65-65.t: And He said ﴿أَوْ يَلْبِسَكُمْ شِيَعاً﴾, because it is from "لَبَسَ", "يَلْبِسُ", "لَبْساً" (to confuse).

akhfash:70-70.t:
And He said ﴿أَن تُبْسَلَ نَفْسٌ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ﴾; it is from "أبْسَلَ", "إبْسالاً" (to give over to destruction).
[And] He said ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُبْسِلُواْ﴾.

akhfash:71-71.t:
As for His saying ﴿حَيْرَانَ لَهُ أَصْحَابٌ﴾: every "فَعْلان" that has a [feminine] "فَعْلى" is a diptote, both as definite and as indefinite.
As for His saying ﴿إِلَى ٱلْهُدَى ٱئْتِنَا﴾, the alif in ﴿ائْتِنا﴾ is a connecting alif (alif waṣl), but after it is a radical hamza, which is the one in "أتَى"; it is the yāʾ in your saying "إيتِنا". But it was not pronounced with hamza when the connecting alif appeared, because the connecting alif has a hamza when one begins with it, and they disliked the meeting of two hamzas.
And He said ﴿وَأُمِرْنَا لِنُسْلِمَ لِرَبِّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾, meaning: we have only been commanded so that we submit to the Lord of the worlds — as He said ﴿وَأُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, i.e. I have been commanded only that.

akhfash:72-72.t: Then He said ﴿وَأَنْ أَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلاةَ وَٱتَّقُوهُ﴾, i.e. and we have been commanded: establish the prayer and fear Him. Or the verb is connected by the lām [in the preceding ﴿لِنُسْلِمَ﴾], and the meaning is "I have been commanded to be", just as it is connected by the lām in His saying ﴿لِرَبِّهِمْ يَرْهَبُونَ﴾.

akhfash:73-73.t:
And He said ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَقُولُ كُن فَيَكُونُ﴾. He said: ﴿يَوْم﴾ is in iḍāfa (genitive construct) with His saying ﴿كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾, and it is accusative, and it has no overt khabar — and Allah knows best; it is according to what I have explained to you.
And likewise ﴿يَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِي ٱلصُّوَرِ﴾. Some read ﴿يَوْمَ يُنْفَحُ في الصُّورِ﴾ and some read ﴿يَنْفُخُ﴾ ﴿عَالِمُ ٱلْغَيْبِ وَٱلشَّهَادَةِ﴾.

akhfash:74-74.t:
And He said ﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ لأَبِيهِ آزَرَ﴾ with fatḥa [i.e. genitive of a diptote] if you make ﴿آزَرَ﴾ a badal (substitute) from ﴿أَبيهِ﴾. It has also been read in the nominative as a vocative, as if he said "O Āzar"*. The poet said [in the rajaz metre; this is the one hundred and ninety-third shāhid]:
إِنَّ عَلَيَّ اللهَ أَنْ تُبايِعا * تُقْتَلَ صُبْحاً أَوْ تَجِيىءَ طائَعا
(I owe it to Allah that you shall swear allegiance — be killed at dawn or come obediently.)
He substituted "تُقْتَلَ صُبْحاً" for "تُبَايِعَ".

akhfash:76-76.t:
And He said ﴿فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْلَّيْلُ﴾, and some read ﴿أَجَنَّ﴾. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the one hundred and ninety-fourth shāhid]:
فَلَمّا أَجَنَّ اللَّيْلُ بِتْنا كَأَنَّنا * علىكَثْرَةِ الأَعْداءِ مُحْتَرِسَانِ
(When the night grew dark we spent the night as though, with the many enemies, we were two on guard.)
And he said [in the rajaz metre; this is the one hundred and ninety-fifth shāhid]:
* أَجَنَّكَ اللَّيلُ وَلَمَّا تَشْتَفِ *
(The night has covered you before you were satisfied.)
He made "الجَنّ" the maṣdar (verbal noun) of "جَنَّ". It may also be right that it is "أَجَنَّ" and that this is its maṣdar, as one says "العَطاء" and "الإعطاء" (giving). As for His saying ﴿أَكْنَنتُمْ فِيۤ أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾, they say for its passive participle "مَكْنُونٌ", and some say "مُكَنّ". You say "كَنَنْتُ الجاريَةَ" (I kept the girl sheltered) when you protected her, and "كَنَنْتُها مِن الشَّمْسِ" and also "أَكْنَنْتُها مِن الشَّمْسِ" (I shielded her from the sun). And they say "هِيَ مَكْنُونَة" and "مُكَنَّةٌ". The poet said [in the basīṭ metre; this is the one hundred and ninety-sixth shāhid]:
قَدْ كُنْتُ أُعْطِيهُمُ مالِي وَأَمْنَحُهُمْ * عِرْضِي وَعِنْدَهُمُ في الصَّدْرِ مَكْنُونُ
(I used to give them my wealth and grant them my honour, while they had [rancour] concealed in the breast.)
because [the tribe of] Qays say "كَنَنْتُ العِلْمَ" (I concealed the knowledge), so it is "مَكْنُونْ"; and the Banū Tamīm say "أَكْنَنْتُ العِلْمَ", so it is "مُكَنُّ"; and "كَنَنْتُ الجارِيَةَ", so she is "مَكْنُونَةٌ". In the Book of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أَوْ أَكْنَنْتُمْ فِيۤ أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾, and He said ﴿كَأَنَّهُنَّ بَيْضٌ مَّكْنُونٌ﴾. The poet said [in the kāmil metre; this is the one hundred and ninety-seventh shāhid]:
قَدْ كُنَّ يَكْنُنَّ الوُجُوهَ تَسَتُّراً * فَاليومَ حينَ بَدَوْنَ للنُّظّارِ
(They used to keep their faces hidden, veiling themselves; but today, when they have appeared to the onlookers…)
And Qays recite it "قَدْكُن يُكْنِنَّ".
And He said ﴿فلمَّآ أَفَلَ﴾: it is from "يَأْفِل", "أُفُولاً" (to set).

akhfash:78-78.t:
As for his saying of the sun ﴿هَـٰذَا رَبِّي﴾, it may be on [the sense of] "this rising thing is my Lord";
or on [the sense] that the sun appeared while they used to mention the lord in their speech, so he said to them ﴿هَـٰذَا رَبّي﴾. This is only a parable he struck for them so that they would know, when it disappeared, that the like of it ought not to be a god, and to guide them to the oneness of Allah and that nothing is like Him. The poet said [in the rajaz metre; this is the one hundred and ninety-eighth shāhid]:
مَكَثْتَ حَوْلاً ثُمَّ جِئْتَ قاشِراً * لا حَمَلَتْ مِنْكَ كِراعٌ حافِرا
(You stayed a whole year, then came [as] a calamity; may no shank of yours ever bear a hoof.)

akhfash:84-85.t: He said ﴿وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِ دَاوُودَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ﴾, meaning: ﴿وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ﴾ ﴿وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِ دَاوُودَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ﴾; and likewise ﴿وَزَكَرِيَّا وَيَحْيَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰ﴾.

akhfash:86-86.t: Some read ﴿وَالْيَسَع﴾ and some read ﴿وَاللَّيْسعَ﴾; we read it with the light [lām].

akhfash:90-90.t: And He said ﴿فَبِهُدَاهُمُ ٱقْتَدِهْ﴾. Everything from the verbs with final yāʾ or wāw, in the jussive position, is paused on with hāʾ, so that it is pronounced as it was.

akhfash:92-92.t: And He said ﴿وَهَـٰذَا كِتَابٌ أَنزَلْنَاهُ مُبَارَكٌ مُّصَدِّقُ ٱلَّذِي﴾ — nominative as a ṣifa (qualifier); it may be made accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) for ﴿أَنْزَلْنَاهُ﴾.

akhfash:93-93.t: And He said ﴿وَٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةُ بَاسِطُوۤاْ أَيْدِيهِمْ أَخْرِجُوۤاْ أَنْفُسَكُمُ﴾: we see that He means "they say ﴿أَخْرِجُوۤاْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾" — and Allah knows best. In His saying ﴿بَاسِطُوۤاْ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ there was an indication of that, because He had informed [us] that they wanted something from them.

akhfash:96-96.t:
And He said ﴿فَالِقُ ٱلإِصْبَاحِ﴾, making it a maṣdar (verbal noun) of "أَصْبَحَ". Some read ﴿فالِقُ الأَصْباحِ﴾, the plural of "الصُّبْح" (morning).
And He said ﴿وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ حُسْبَاناً﴾, i.e. by reckoning; He dropped the bāʾ as He dropped it from His saying ﴿أَعْلَمُ مَن يَضِلُّ عَن سَبِيلِهِ﴾, i.e. He knows best about (بمن) the one who strays. "الحُسْبان" is the plural of "الحِساب", like "شِهاب" and "شُهْبَان"; and like it is "الشَمْسُ والقَمرُ بِحُسْبانٍ", i.e. by reckoning.

akhfash:98-98.t: And He said ﴿أَنْشَأَكُم مِّن نَّفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ فَمُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمُسْتَوْدَعٌ﴾: we see that He means: of them is one settled and of them is one deposited — and Allah knows best. And it is [also] read ﴿مُسْتَقَرّ﴾. [Translator's note: the gloss has «مُسْتَقِرٌّ» (with kasra) for the first reading; the text writes the second reading the same as the verse as quoted.]

akhfash:99-99.t:
And He said ﴿فَأَخْرَجْنَا مِنْهُ خَضِراً﴾, meaning "الأَخْضَر" (green), as in the Arabs' saying "أرِنيِها نَمِرَةً أُرِكَها مَطِرَةً" (show me it [the cloud] spotted, and I will show it to you rainy).
And He said ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلنَّخْلِ مِن طَلْعِهَا قِنْوَانٌ دَانِيَةٌ﴾, then He said ﴿وَجَنَّاتٍ مِّنْ أَعْنَابٍ﴾, i.e. "and We brought forth by it gardens of grapes".
Then He said ﴿وَٱلزَّيْتُونَ﴾. The singular of "القِنْوان" is "قِنْوٌ" (date cluster), and likewise "الصِّنْوان", whose singular is "صِنْوٌ".

akhfash:100-100.t:
And He said ﴿وَجَعَلُواْ للَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ ٱلْجِنَّ﴾ as a badal (substitute), as He said ﴿إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ صِرَاطِ ٱللَّهِ ﴾. The poet said [in the wāfir metre; this is the two hundredth shāhid]:
ذَرِينِي إِنَّ أمرَكِ لَن يُطاعا * وَمَا ألفَيْتِني حِلْمِي مُضاعا
(Leave me, for your command will not be obeyed, and you have not found me — my forbearance — lost.)
And he said [in the basīṭ metre; this is the two hundred and first shāhid]:
إِنِّي وَجَدْتُكَ يا جُرْثُومُ مِنْ نَفَرٍ * جُرْثُومَةِ اللُّؤْمِ لا جُرْثُومَةِ الكَرَمِ
(I have found you, O Jurthūm, to be of a clan whose root is baseness, not the root of nobility.)
[And another said] [in the basīṭ metre; this is the one hundred and fifty-fifth shāhid]:
إِنَّا وَجَدْنا بَنِي جِلاّنَ كُلَّهم * كساعِد الضُّبِّ لا طُولٌ ولا عِظَمُ*
(We found the Banū Jillān, all of them, like the forearm of a lizard — neither length nor bulk.)
And he said [in the rajaz metre; this is the two hundred and second shāhid]:
ما لِلجِمالِ مَشْيِها وَئيدا * أَجَنْدَلاً لاَ يَحْمِلْنَ أَمْ حَدِيدا
(What is the matter with the camels, their walking so slowly? Is it stones they carry, or iron?)
And one also says "ما للجمالِ مشيُها وَئيدا" [with the nominative], as was said [in the wāfir metre; this is the two hundred and third shāhid]:
فكيفَ تَرَى عَطِيَّةَ حِينَ تَلْقَى * عِظاماً هامُهُنَّ قُرآسِيات
(So how do you see ʿAṭiyya when he meets great ones whose heads are massive?)

akhfash:105-105.t: And His saying ﴿وَلِيَقُولُواْ دَرَسْتَ﴾, i.e. you studied with the People of the Book; ﴿وَكَذٰلِكَ نُصَرِّفُ ٱلآيَاتِ﴾ means: thus. Some read ﴿دَرَسْتَ﴾, and that is how we read it, because it accords better with the Book. And some read ﴿دَرَسَتْ﴾. [Translator's note: the first reading was evidently «دَارَسْتَ», as the gloss shows; the text writes it as ﴿دَرَسْتَ﴾.]

akhfash:108-108.t: And He said ﴿فَيَسُبُّواْ ٱللَّهَ عَدُوّاً بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾, heavy, doubled; and ﴿عَدْواً﴾ light, the origin being from "العُدْوان" (aggression). Some read ﴿عَدُوّاً﴾ without knowledge, i.e. they reviled Him in this state; but "العَدُوّ" is a collective, as He said ﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لِيۤ﴾ and as He said ﴿لاَ تَتَّخِذُواْ عَدُوِّي وَعَدُوَّكُمْ أَوْلِيَآءَ﴾. We read ﴿عَدْواً﴾ because it is more frequent in the reading and better in meaning, since you say "[عُدا] عَدْواً علينا" (he committed aggression against us), like "ضَرَبَهُ ضَرْباً" (he struck him a striking).

akhfash:109-109.t:
And He said ﴿وَمَا يُشْعِرُكُمْ أَنَّهَآ إِذَا جَآءَتْ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾. Some read ﴿أَنَّها﴾, and that is how we read it, and it was explained as "لعلها" (perhaps it), as the Arabs say "اِذْهَبْ إِلى السوق أَنَّكَ تشتري لي شيئاً" (go to the market — perhaps you will buy me something), i.e. perhaps you. The poet said [in the rajaz metre; this is the one hundred and ninety-ninth shāhid]:
قُلْتُ لِشَيْبانَ اذْنُ من لِقائِهِ * أَنَّا نُغَذِّي القَوَمَ مِن شِوائِه
(I said to Shaybān: draw near to meet it — perhaps we will feed the people from its roast.)
in the sense of "لَعَلَّنا" (perhaps we).

akhfash:111-111.t: He said ﴿وَحَشَرْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ قُبُلاً﴾, i.e. group by group; "القُبُل" is the plural of "القَبيل" (group). One also says "قِبَلا", i.e. face to face. And He said ﴿أَوْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ قُبُلاً﴾, i.e. face to face. You say "لا قِبَلَ لي بهذا", i.e. I have no power [for this]*. And you say "لِي قِبَلَك حقٌ" (I have a claim on you), i.e. with you.

akhfash:113-113.t: [And] He said ﴿وَلِتَصْغَىۤ إِلَيْهِ أَفْئِدَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلآخِرَةِ﴾: it is from "صَغَوْتُ", "يَصْغا" (to incline), like "مَحَوْتُ", "يُمْحا".

akhfash:119-119.t:
And He said ﴿وَمَا لَكُمْ أَلاَّ تَأْكُلُواْ مِمَّا ذُكِرَ ٱسْمُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ﴾, meaning — and Allah knows best — "what [reason] do you have for not eating?". Likewise ﴿وَمَا لَنَآ أَلاّ نُقَاتِلَ﴾ means: "what [reason] do we have for abandoning fighting?". If ﴿أَنْ﴾ were zāʾida (redundant), the verb would be nominative; and if it were in the sense of "what have we to do with such-and-such", it would be "وَمَالَنا وَأَلاّ نُقَاتِلَ".
And He said ﴿وَإِنَّ كَثِيراً لَّيُضِلُّونَ بِأَهْوَائِهِم﴾, and it is read ﴿ليُضِلُّونَ﴾. He made "أنَّ" fall on an indefinite noun because when speech is long it bears [this], and one part of it indicates another.

akhfash:123-123.t: And He said ﴿وَكَذٰلِكَ جَعَلْنَا فِي كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ أَكَابِرَ مُجَرِمِيهَا لِيَمْكُرُواْ فِيهَا﴾: He built it on [the pattern] "أَفاعِل", because it occurs in two ways: one says "هؤلاء الأكابر" and "الأكبرون". And He said ﴿نُنَبِّئُكُم بِٱلأَخْسَرِينَ أَعْمَالاً﴾, whose singular is "أَخْسَرُ", like "الأَكْبَر".

akhfash:137-137.t:
And He said ﴿وَكَذٰلِكَ زَيَّنَ لِكَثِيرٍ مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ قَتْلَ أَوْلاَدِهِمْ شُرَكَآؤُهُمْ﴾, because the partners made [it] seem fair.
Then He said ﴿لِيُرْدُوهُمْ﴾, from "أرْدى", "إِرْداءَ" (to destroy).

akhfash:138-138.t: And He said ﴿حِجْرٌ لاَّ يَطْعَمُهَآ﴾: "الحِجْر" is "the forbidden". It has also been read with ḍamma, ﴿حُجْرٌ﴾; and likewise ﴿حُجْراً مَحْجُورا﴾ has been read with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ, and ﴿حِجْراً﴾, with one meaning. "الحِجْر" may also be intellect; Allah the Exalted said ﴿هَلْ فِي ذَلِكَ قَسَمٌ لِّذِى حِجْرٍ﴾, i.e. one possessed of intellect. Some said: "In His saying ﴿وَحَرْثٌ حِجْرٌ﴾ there can only be kasra." This is nothing, because it means forbidden. As for "حجْرُ المرأة" (a woman's lap), it has fatḥa and kasra; and "حَجْرُ اليَمامة"* is with fatḥa; and "الحِجْرُ" is what you have enclosed, and it is [as in] the saying ﴿أصْحابِ الحجر﴾.

akhfash:139-139.t: And the saying of [Allah] the Mighty and Majestic ﴿وَقَالُواْ مَا فِي بُطُونِ هَـٰذِهِ ٱلأَنْعَامِ خَالِصَةٌ لِّذُكُورِنَا وَمُحَرَّمٌ عَلَىٰ أَزْوَاجِنَا وَإِن يَكُن مَّيْتَةً فَهُمْ فِيهِ شُرَكَآءُ﴾ — nominative, i.e.**: and if there is in their bellies a dead [foetus]. The nominative is permissible when you say ﴿يَكُن﴾ [with yāʾ], because the verb of a feminine may be made masculine. And ﴿خالِصَةٌ﴾ was made feminine to intensify the exclusiveness: as if, when He intensified the exclusiveness for them, it resembled abundance, so it was treated like "رَاوِية" (great transmitter) and "نَسّابة" (great genealogist).

akhfash:141-141.t: [And He said] ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾ — genitive [in form], because the tāʾ of the [feminine] plural in the accusative position is genitive with tanwīn.

akhfash:142-142.t: Then He said ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلأَنْعَامِ حَمُولَةً وَفَرْشاً﴾, i.e. and He produced of the livestock beasts of burden and small ones.

akhfash:143-143.t:
Then He said ﴿ثَمَانِيَةَ أَزْوَاجٍ﴾, i.e. He produced beasts of burden and small ones, eight pairs, i.e. He produced eight pairs — as a badal (substitute), or as an explication (tibyān), or as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
Then He said: He produced ﴿مِنَ ٱلضَّأْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَمِنَ ٱلْمَعْزِ ٱثْنَيْنِ﴾. He only said ﴿ثَمَانِيَةَ أَزْوَاجٍ﴾ because each one is a "زَوْج" (mate). You say of two: "هذانِ زَوْجانِ" (these are two mates). Allah the Mighty and Majestic said ﴿وَمِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَا زَوْجَيْنِ﴾. You say of a woman: "هي زَوْجٌ" and "هي زَوْجَةٌ" (she is a wife), and "هو زَوْجُها" (he is her husband). He said ﴿وَجَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَها﴾, meaning the woman, and He said ﴿أَمْسِكْ عَلَيْكَ زَوْجَكَ﴾. Some say "الزَوْجَة". al-Akhṭal said [in the basīṭ metre; this is the one hundred and twenty-seventh shāhid]:
زَوْجَةُ أَشْمَطَ مَرْهُوبٌ بَوادِرُهُ * قَدْ صار في رَأْسِهِ التَخْوِيصَ والنَزَعُ
(The wife of a grizzled man whose outbursts are feared, on whose head greyness and baldness have appeared.)
[Translator's note: the text has «السابع والشعرون», evidently for «السابع والعشرون» "twenty-seventh"; this and the next number are out of the sequence of this section.] One may also say of two: "هما زَوْجٌ" (they are a pair). [And "الزَوْجُ" is the patterned cloth thrown over the camel-litter.] Labīd said [in the kāmil metre; this is the one hundred and twenty-sixth shāhid]:
مِنْ كُلِّ محْفُوفٍ يُظِلُّ عِصِيَّهُ * زَوْجٌ عَلَيْهِ كِلَّةٌ وقِرامُها
(From every curtained litter whose poles are shaded by a cloth, with a canopy and its screen upon it.)
As for ﴿الضَأن﴾ (sheep), it has hamza, and it is a plural without a singular [of its own form]. One also says ﴿الضَئِين﴾, like "الشَعِير", and it is the plural of "الضَأْن"; the female is "ضائِنَة" and the plural "الضَوَائِن".
And ﴿المَعْزُ﴾ (goats) is a plural without a singular, and likewise "المِعْزَى". As for "المَواعِز", its singular is "الماعِز" and "الماعِزَة". The single male is "ضائِنْ", so "الضَأْن" is the plural of "الضائِنْ", like "صاحِب" and "صَحْب", "تاجِر" and "تَجْر"; and likewise "ماعِزْ" and "مَعْز". Some read ﴿ضأَنْ﴾ and ﴿مَعَز﴾, making it the plural of "الضَائِن" and "الماعِز", like "خَادِم" and "خَدَم"; and "حافِد" and "حَفَدَةْ" is like it, except that the hāʾ has been added to it.
As for His saying ﴿َآلذَّكَرَيْنِ حَرَّمَ أَمِ ٱلأُنثَيَيْنِ﴾, it is accusative by "حرّم" (He forbade).

akhfash:145-145.t: And He said ﴿فَإِنَّهُ رِجْسٌ أَوْ فِسْقاً﴾, meaning: "unless it be carrion … or an abomination — for it is filth".

akhfash:146-146.t: And He said ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلْبَقَرِ وَٱلْغَنَمِ حَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ شُحُومَهُمَآ إِلاَّ مَا حَمَلَتْ ظُهُورُهُمَا أَوِ ٱلْحَوَايَآ﴾. The singular of "الحَوايا" (entrails) is "الحاوِياء" and "الحَاوِيَة". By His saying ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلْبَقَرِ وَٱلْغَنَمِ﴾ He means — and Allah knows best — "and the cattle and sheep, We forbade to them"; but He put "مِنْ" in it. The Arabs say "قَدْ كانَ مِنْ حَديثٍ" meaning "there has been talk". And if you wish, you say "وَمِنْ الغَنَمِ حَرَّمْنا الشُّحُومَ" (and of the sheep We forbade the fats), as you say "مِنَ الدّارِ أُخِذَ النِّصفُ والثُلُثُ" (of the house, half and a third were taken); so you attached [the pronoun by iḍāfa] in this sense, as you say "مِنَ الدّارِ أُخِذَ نِصْفُها" (of the house, its half was taken) and "مِنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ ضُرِبَ وَجْهُهُ" (of ʿAbdullāh, his face was struck).

akhfash:150-150.t: And He said ﴿هَلُمَّ شُهَدَآءَكُمُ﴾, because "هَلُمَّ" may be used for the singular, the dual and the plural.

akhfash:156-156.t: And He said ﴿أَن تَقُولُوۤاْ إِنَّمَآ أُنزِلَ ٱلْكِتَابُ عَلَىٰ طَآئِفَتَيْنِ مِن قَبْلِنَا﴾ [depending] on ﴿ثُمَّ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى ٱلْكِتَابَ﴾ — out of dislike that ﴿أَن تَقُولُوۤاْ إِنَّمَآ أُنزِلَ ٱلْكِتَابُ عَلَىٰ طَآئِفَتَيْنِ مِن قَبْلِنَا﴾.

akhfash:159-159.t: And He said ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ فَرَّقُواْ دِينَهُمْ وَكَانُواْ شِيَعاً﴾, and some read ﴿فارَقُوا﴾, from "المُفارَقَة" (departing).

akhfash:160-160.t: And He said ﴿فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا﴾ as a number, as you say "عَشْرُ سُودٍ" (ten black ones). If you ask how He said "عَشْر" [the form used with feminine nouns] when "المِثْل" is masculine: He only used the feminine because it is attached by iḍāfa to a feminine [pronoun], and in meaning too it is "حَسَنَةٌ" (a good deed) or "دَرَجةٌ" (a degree); if He used the feminine on that basis, it is a [valid] way. Some read ﴿عَشْرٌ أمْثالُها﴾, making "الأمثال" a qualifier of "العشر". This is the [proper] way, except that it is not read, because a number is not put in iḍāfa with what is a qualifier; rather one says "هُمْ عَشْرَةٌ قيامٌ" (they are ten, standing) and "عشرةٌ قُعُودٌ" (ten, sitting); one does not say "عشرةُ قيامٍ".

akhfash:161-161.t: And He said ﴿دِيناً قِيَماً﴾, i.e. upright; this is the reading of the generality. The people of Medina read ﴿قِيَما﴾, and it is good, though I have not heard it from the Arabs; it is in the meaning [as] explained. [Translator's note: both readings are written identically here; the reading of the generality was evidently «قَيِّماً».]
